In [[mathematics]], or more specifically in [[spectral theory]], the '''Riesz projector''' is the projector onto the eigenspace corresponding to a particular [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalue]] of an operator (or, more generally, a projector onto an [[invariant subspace]] corresponding to an isolated part of the spectrum). It was introduced by [[Frigyes Riesz]] in 1912.<ref>{{ cite book 
|title=Functional Analysis
|author1=Riesz, F.
|author2=Sz.-Nagy, B.
|publisher = Blackie & Son Limited
|year =      1956
|url =http://gen.lib.rus.ec/book/index.php?md5=0B8573C90CF9D9A0E51B0746BCB22452
}}</ref><ref>{{ cite book
|author1=Gohberg, I. C
|author2=Kreĭn, M. G.
|title=Introduction to the theory of linear nonselfadjoint operators
|year=1969
|publisher = American Mathematical Society, Providence, R.I.
|url=http://gen.lib.rus.ec/book/index.php?md5=9CE2F03854312C3E29ED684CD84D8CA3
}}
</ref>

==Definition==
Let <math>A</math> be a [[Unbounded operator#Closed linear operators|closed linear operator]] in the Banach space <math>\mathfrak{B}</math>. Let <math>\Gamma</math> be  a simple or composite rectifiable contour, which encloses some region <math>G_\Gamma</math> and lies entirely within the [[resolvent set]] <math>\rho(A)</math> (<math>\Gamma\subset\rho(A)</math>) of the operator <math>A</math>. Assuming that the contour <math>\Gamma</math> has a positive orientation with respect to the region <math>G_\Gamma</math>, the Riesz projector corresponding to <math>\Gamma</math> is defined by
:<math>
P_\Gamma=-\frac{1}{2\pi \mathrm{i}}\oint_\Gamma(A-z I_{\mathfrak{B}})^{-1}\,\mathrm{d}z;
</math>
here <math>I_{\mathfrak{B}}</math> is the [[identity operator]] in <math>\mathfrak{B}</math>.

If <math>\lambda\in\sigma(A)</math> is the only point of the spectrum of <math>A</math> in <math>G_\Gamma</math>, then <math>P_\Gamma</math> is denoted by <math>P_\lambda</math>.

==Properties==
The operator <math>P_\Gamma</math> is a projector which commutes with <math>A</math>, and hence in the decomposition
:<math>\mathfrak{B}=\mathfrak{L}_\Gamma\oplus\mathfrak{N}_\Gamma
\qquad
\mathfrak{L}_\Gamma=P_\Gamma\mathfrak{B},
\quad
\mathfrak{N}_\Gamma=(I_{\mathfrak{B}}-P_\Gamma)\mathfrak{B},
</math>
both terms <math>\mathfrak{L}_\Gamma</math> and <math>\mathfrak{N}_\Gamma</math> are [[invariant subspace]]s of the operator <math>A</math>.
Moreover,
# The spectrum of the restriction of <math>A</math> to the subspace <math>\mathfrak{L}_\Gamma</math> is contained in the region <math>G_\Gamma</math>;
# The spectrum of the restriction of <math>A</math> to the subspace <math>\mathfrak{N}_\Gamma</math> lies outside the closure of <math>G_\Gamma</math>.

If <math>\Gamma_1</math> and <math>\Gamma_2</math> are two different contours having the properties indicated above, and the regions  <math>G_{\Gamma_1}</math>
and <math>G_{\Gamma_2}</math> have no points in common, then the projectors corresponding to them are mutually orthogonal:
:<math>
P_{\Gamma_1}P_{\Gamma_2}
=
P_{\Gamma_2}P_{\Gamma_1}=0.
</math>
